newsitem.title: UK: Glaxo extends decline as ADRs retreat.
newsitem.headline: Glaxo extends decline as ADRs retreat.

text.p: Shares in Glaxo Wellcome Plc dropped on Wednesday, as its ADRs fell in New York in line with mostly weak U.S. drug stocks and following cautious comment on the stock from Dresdner Kleinwort Benson, dealers said.
Glaxo shares were down 14p at 11.91 stg by 1416 GMT, in volume of 2.9 million shares. Its ADRs were down $1/2 at $38-5/8, after on Tuesday falling $5/8 to $39-1/8.

Analyst Peter McDougal, recently recruited to Kleinwort from BZW, repeated Kleinwort's existing "weak hold" rating on Glaxo but advised investors not to sell the stock pending possible positive news on its blockbuster ulcer drug Zantac in the U.S.

Noting that Novartis had sought six months exclusive rights to sell a generic version of Zantac, McDougal said a postive outcome for Swiss company would support Zantac prices in the U.S. in the short term and could give Glaxo shares a boost.
Kleinwort's "weak hold" rating reflects the brokerage's view on Glaxo's longer-term growth prospects, dealers said.
Glaxo's U.S. patent on Zantac expires in July.
